'''Denis A. Higgs''' ({{Birth date|df=yes|1932|5|6}} – {{Death date|2011|2|25}}) was a British mathematician, Doctor of Mathematics, and professor of mathematics who specialised in [[combinatorics]], [[universal algebra]], and [[category theory]]. He wrote one of the most influential papers in [[category theory]] entitled ''A category approach to boolean valued set theory'', which introduced many students to [[topos|topos theory]].<ref name=ps>{{cite web|url= http://permalink.gmane.org/gmane.science.mathematics.categories/6574|title= Denis Higgs|last1= Scott|first1= Phil|date= 7 March 2011|publisher= Mount Allison University|access-date= 14 December 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000035/http://permalink.gmane.org/gmane.science.mathematics.categories/6574|archive-date= 4 March 2016|url-status= dead}}</ref>
He was a member of the [[African Resistance Movement|National Committee of Liberation]] and was an outspoken critic against the [[apartheid in South Africa]].

==Life==

He earned degrees from [[Cambridge University]], St John's College, in England, [[University of the Witwatersrand]] in South Africa, and [[McMaster University]] in Canada.<ref name="mathgenealogy"/>

In 1962, he became a member of the [[African Resistance Movement|National Committee of Liberation]], a movement whose main objective was to dismantle the [[apartheid in South Africa]].<ref name=sade>{{cite book|title=The Road to Democracy in South Africa (1960–1970)|author= South African Democracy Education Trust|isbn= 9781868729067|lccn= 2004448218|series= The Road to Democracy in South Africa|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=qIQttVhKf3EC|year= 2004|publisher= Zebra Press}}</ref>

On 28 August 1964, he was kidnapped from his home in [[Lusaka]], Zambia. Then South Africa's Justice Minister [[John Vorster]], who later became Prime Minister, denied any involvement by either the South African government or the police, but accused Higgs of being an accessory to the [[Frederick John Harris|bombing that killed Ethel Rhys]] and wounded many others.<ref name=news>{{cite news |title= Kidnapped Teacher Goes Back to Rhodesia|url= https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1301&dat=19640903&id=2kUjAAAAIBAJ&pg=2839,4269434|newspaper= The Sydney Morning Herald|date= 3 September 1964|access-date=7 December 2012}}</ref>

On 1 September, an unidentified man who claimed to be part of British Protectorates called the [[The Rand Daily Mail|''Rand Daily Mail'' newspaper]] and gave specific details of Denis Higgs's whereabouts. On 2 September, police authorities found him. He was blindfolded and bound in a van over by the Zoo Park area. Although Higgs was wanted for the [[Johannesburg]] railway bombing that killed Rhys, authorities declined to prosecute since Higgs had been returned to South Africa via an extrajudicial kidnapping rather than proper extradition channels.<ref name=news/>

After first leaving South Africa to return to Zambia, on 6 September 1964, Higgs fled to London, accompanied by his family. He later stated that he feared for his safety and that of his family, since a day before his departure, the South African government had begun proceedings of extradition for his alleged participation in the explosion at the Johannesburg Railway Station that killed Rhys.<ref name=sade/>

==Career==

He emigrated to Canada in 1966, earning a doctorate from McMaster,<ref name="mathgenealogy"/> and held a position as a professor of Pure Mathematics at the [[University of Waterloo]], where he wrote one of the most influential papers in [[category theory]] entitled ''A category approach to boolean valued set theory'', which introduced many students to [[topos|topos theory]].<ref name="ps"/>

In 1973, he generalised the Rasiowa-Sikorski Boolean models to the case of [[category theory]].<ref>{{cite book|title= Andrzej Mostowski and Foundational Studies|last1= Mostowski |first1 = A.  |last2 = Ehrenfeucht |first2 = A.  |last3 = Marek |first3 = V.W.|last4 = Srebrny |first4 = M.|isbn= 9781586037826|lccn= 2007939570|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=Ri4kjs-iGRgC|year= 2008|publisher= Ios Press Inc}}</ref>

His academic papers were published in ''[[Algebra Universalis]]'', the ''[[Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra]]'', the ''[[Australian Mathematical Society#Society journals|Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society]]'', the ''[[London Mathematical Society#Publications|Journal of the London Mathematical Society]]'', and ''[[Mathematics of Computation]]'', among other journals.

He died on 25 February 2011.<ref>{{cite journal|journal= Notices of the American Mathematical Society|title= Notices of the AMS|publisher = American Mathematical Society|volume = 58|year = 2011|issue = 5|page = 731|url = https://www.ams.org/notices/201105/rtx110500730p.pdf}}</ref>
